works.title: Centering / Shuttering (Formwork)
works.description: Practical site-readiness and execution knowledge for formwork/shuttering, linked to the existing governed reusable work identity and QA hold-point template.

Labor: Skilled formwork / shuttering carpenter or equivalent competent formwork worker
Helpers for handling, cleaning, lifting and positioning
Foreman / supervisor as required by the site organization
Tools: Measuring tape, marker / pencil and chalk line
Spirit level / laser level and plumb checking tools
Hammer, nail puller / pry bar and general hand tools
Saw / cutting tools suitable for the selected formwork system
Drill / driver, spanners and clamps where the system requires them
Equipment: Approved props / jacks / support system as applicable
Safe scaffolding, working platforms and access ladders where required
Lifting / handling equipment where panel weight or site conditions require it
Materials: Approved plywood, boards or proprietary formwork panels for the selected system
Timber / steel / aluminium secondary members, walers and supports as applicable
Ties, clamps, nails, screws and connection accessories required by the selected system
Joint sealing material / foam / tape where required by the approved detail
Safety: Edge / fall protection where there is fall exposure
Stable support, bracing and base bearing before loading
Housekeeping and controlled lifting / electrical-tool use
Preconditions: Latest approved structural / architectural drawings and dimensions are available
Formwork arrangement / support plan is resolved where design is required
Bearing surface and support locations are stable and suitable
Rebar, openings, sleeves, embeds and MEP interfaces are coordinated
Panels / contact surfaces are clean and release-agent requirements are understood
Pre-pour formwork inspection / hold point is planned

wms.title: Review drawings and formwork system
wms.note: Confirm dimensions, levels, openings, supports, interfaces and the approved formwork method before fabrication/erection.

wms.title: Prepare panels and support components
wms.note: Clean, inspect, cut/assemble and stage the selected formwork components without inventing unapproved member sizes or spacings.

wms.title: Set out line and level
wms.note: Transfer the required lines, dimensions and levels before fixing the formwork.

wms.title: Erect, support and brace
wms.note: Install panels, props, ties, walers and bracing in accordance with the approved system / design.

wms.title: Check geometry and tightness
wms.note: Verify dimensions, line, level, plumb, joints, openings and leakage-prone gaps.

wms.title: Coordinate embeds and reinforcement interfaces
wms.note: Confirm sleeves, inserts, openings, reinforcement clearances and other concealed interfaces before closure.

wms.title: Release-agent / cleanliness check
wms.note: Confirm contact surfaces are clean and approved release agent is correctly applied without contaminating reinforcement or construction joints.

wms.title: Pre-pour inspection
wms.note: Do not permit concrete placement until the governed formwork hold point is accepted.

wms.title: Monitor during concrete placement
wms.note: Observe formwork movement, leakage, bracing and supports during placement; stop/escalate if unsafe or unstable conditions appear.

wms.title: Strip, clean and stack
wms.note: Remove formwork only after approved stripping/strength criteria are satisfied; clean, inspect and store reusable components.

works.wms_notice: This knowledge page does not assert prop spacing, tie spacing, panel thickness, stripping time, concrete-pressure limits or other design values. Those must come from the approved formwork design/system, project documents and applicable engineering requirements.

itp.criteria: Dimensions, line, level and plumb match approved drawings.
Supports, base bearing, ties, clamps and bracing are stable and appropriate to the approved system.
Joints, cleanliness and release-agent condition are acceptable before concrete.
Openings, sleeves, embeds and reinforcement/MEP interfaces are coordinated before closure.
Formwork is accepted before concrete placement.
Removal follows approved strength/time/project criteria and does not damage the concrete.

field_notes: Field-knowledge principle: the page should answer what labour, tools, equipment, materials, safety controls and preconditions the site needs before starting work.
Future site-team additions should remain visibly tagged as FIELD KNOWLEDGE until they are reconciled with project/design/codal authority.

mapping.IFC: Reusable work knowledge can map to task type; real project formwork activity remains an activity occurrence
mapping.P6: Schedule activity links through work_id, not by copying WMS text into P6

works.title: Cementitious Waterproofing
works.description: Mapped example showing how practical site readiness, method, inspection and open-standard mappings attach to one reusable work identity.

Labor: Contractor-provided labour requirement is kept separate from tools and materials.
Preconditions: Access, weather, water and power readiness checked

wms.title: Authority & scope check
wms.note: Confirm approved drawing/specification/product system and project-specific method before work.

wms.title: Substrate readiness
wms.note: Inspect and prepare substrate; record defects before proceeding.

wms.title: Repairs & interfaces
wms.note: Treat joints, cracks, corners, penetrations and drains only to approved detail.

wms.title: Application sequence
wms.note: Follow approved project/manufacturer method; no demo thickness, mix ratio or curing time is invented.

wms.title: Inspection / test
wms.note: Complete governed test/inspection before covering.

wms.title: Protection & records
wms.note: Protect accepted work and link evidence to the real execution identity.

works.wms_notice: Illustrative workflow only. Numerical requirements must come from verified project specifications, manufacturer requirements and applicable authoritative standards.

itp.criteria: Approved references, substrate and interfaces verified.
Work follows approved system; deviations are recorded.
Required inspection/test passes and real evidence is linked.

works.title: Construction of Soak Pit
works.description: Fail-closed research example. Identity and numerical technical requirements stay unresolved until live catalogue/design/codal authority is verified.

Labor: Crew requirement pending approved execution plan.
Equipment: Excavation/dewatering/access equipment only if verified site conditions require it
Materials: Stone/aggregate/masonry/pipe/cover/filter materials only after design/specification verification

wms.title: Resolve work identity
wms.note: Check governed work catalogue/BOQ before creating a new work_id.

wms.title: Verify design basis
wms.note: Resolve hydraulic basis, site suitability and governing authority.

wms.title: Clause-level research
wms.note: Trace every numerical requirement to source, edition, clause/table/figure and applicability.

wms.title: Develop construction sequence
wms.note: Only then define setting out, excavation, base/walls/inlet/cover/backfill/inspection/as-built steps.

wms.title: Engineering review of local practice
wms.note: The user-supplied two-rebar alternative remains unapproved until structural/durability/detail checks are complete.

works.wms_notice: No soak-pit dimension, mortar ratio, weep-hole spacing, reinforcement size or separation distance is asserted by this demo.

itp.criteria: Applicable design and authority requirements resolved.
Actual soil, groundwater, utility and safe-excavation conditions recorded.
Real inspection, photos/as-built and acceptance captured.
